markdown_report:
SASRec offers three starting insights: causal attention can represent changing interests, yet stale evidence remains a diagnosed concern; dot products encode associations without establishing compatibility; sampled BCE can separate easy pairs while difficult rankings remain unresolved. Electronics has 14.95% wrong pairwise rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin. Embedding similarity near 0.5 provides little evidence for prioritizing collapse remedies.

Related work provides three directions: TGCL4SR motivates global/local collaborative evidence; LS4SRec motivates separating recent and persistent interests; gSASRec motivates testing sampling and calibration together. These works establish neither gains here nor that collaborative transitions identify practical fit.

| Component | Evidence | Intended contribution | Unresolved limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Ordered personal history | Personalized sequence representation | Unsupported associations |
| Directed transitions | Consecutive training interactions | Plausible next-step evidence | Association is not compatibility |
| Co-occurrence | Binary training-user incidence | Repeated collaborative support | Popularity and rare coincidences |
| Recency weighting | Relative interaction position | Current-interest emphasis | Position is an imperfect clock |
| Loss calibration | Sampled scores | Difficult-case separation | Unobserved items may be relevant |

Three atomic candidates remain. O/F/U/M/D denote originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Candidate | O/F/U/M/D | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent transition residual | 3/6/7/7/5 | Tests collaborative support and recency with frozen SASRec | Established ensemble; graph diagnostics add complexity |
| Learned recent/history gate | 4/7/8/6/5 | Direct temporal adaptation | Sparse routing evidence; added optimization |
| Warm-start multi-negative loss | 3/7/4/8/4 | Targets weak separation | Does not explicitly address two user failures |

Select **recent transition residual** at 0% progress, with reduced novelty/potential ratings and increased implementation difficulty. It targets unsupported broad matches through observed next-step support and stale isolated interests through recent weighting. Its model-facing target is lower-tail ranking confusion, particularly Electronics. Compatibility, satisfied needs, and immediate acceptance remain unobserved; improvements are hypotheses.

Construct training-only directed counts and cosine ItemKNN, normalize before source-row top-K, and freeze training-derived score scales. Blend recent-history graph scores with SASRec using a tiny shared grid containing zero. ItemKNN and sequential-rule references clarify that this is an established neighborhood ensemble, not a new graph architecture.

Preserve identical pinned validation candidates. Ablate branches and popularity; report coverage, rescues/regressions, category deltas, history/popularity strata, and paired bootstrap uncertainty. Record every inspected configuration: selection intervals remain optimistic. Compare matched-negative BCE/gBCE when budget permits, then test one preregistered ensemble on the stronger comparator.

Diagnostics must score each causal prefix through the complete hybrid. Report ordinary training-graph margins alongside graph-only user-exclusion margins where user identity is recoverable; target inclusion can inflate training fit. Exclusion removes all user contributions and recomputes normalization/pruning, while neural parameters remain unchanged. The anonymous loader cannot silently supply user identity. Use pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection; training margins and sampled rankings do not establish full-catalog quality.

idea.description: Add a sparse, recency-weighted collaborative residual to each category’s SASRec scores. Directed transitions supply observed next-step associations, and cosine ItemKNN supplies collaborative support. Select a small shared blend configuration using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Treat the method as a neighborhood/transition ensemble with limited architectural novelty.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies unsupported broad associations and excessive influence from older or isolated interactions. Recent collaborative evidence explicitly targets both patterns, although it can also reproduce them and must be validated. The quantitative target is weak lower-tail positive–negative separation, most pronounced in Electronics. Implicit interactions cannot establish equipment compatibility, replacement need, satisfied demand, or simulator traits. Scores near 0.5 on the mapped embedding-similarity diagnostic do not establish severe collapse.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four categories and dataset routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], the original splits, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write checkpoints, sparse tables, score scales, configuration manifests, and the predictor beneath the trial directory. Do not inspect hidden tests, obtain pretrained weights, use excluded metadata/reviews, or alter the evaluator. All training and diagnostics count toward the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; operate on one GPU.

For each category, retain chronological training histories. Build binary deduplicated user–item incidence X, item supports d, and C=X.T@X. Define cosine similarities C_ij/sqrt(d_i*d_j), clear the diagonal, and retain the largest K=100 similarities per source row AFTER normalization. Do not renormalize cosine rows after pruning. Directed counts include every adjacent chronological training event, including repeated events; explicitly remove self-transitions. Divide each transition count by its source's total remaining outgoing count BEFORE retaining source-row top-100 entries; do not renormalize afterward. A source without outgoing mass contributes zero. Pruning can break cosine symmetry. Use bounded sparse blocks for co-occurrence products and monitor intermediate nonzeros; never materialize a dense catalog-square matrix. Fix block sizing from memory constraints rather than validation accuracy.

At inference, use the last W=10 nonpadding interactions, weighting positions by exp(-age/3) and normalizing weights to sum to one. Preserve repeated source occurrences. Empty histories receive zero graph scores. Aggregate outgoing transition and cosine rows for arbitrary candidate IDs. Fit a separate standard deviation for each scoring branch and category from at most 10,000 training prefixes, sampled with a dedicated seed-42 generator, each paired with 32 uniformly sampled items excluding that user's training items. Bound each standard deviation below by 1e-6 and divide scores by it; omit centering because candidate-independent offsets do not change rankings. Freeze these scales before validation and reuse them for sampled and full-catalog inference. Do not normalize over evaluator candidates. If a branch is identically zero, disable it and record that fact.

Prespecify the shared grid (transition weight, co-occurrence weight)={(0,0),(0.1,0),(0,0.1),(0.1,0.1),(0.3,0),(0,0.3),(0.3,0.3)}. Use one shared pair across all four datasets, with category-specific fixed scales. Freeze the original baseline checkpoint-selection rule and training settings before comparisons; document that rule exactly in the manifest and do not tune it alongside blend weights. If the baseline has no checkpoint-selection rule, use the final configured epoch. Break equal macro HR@10 by smaller total blend weight, then lexicographic order. Zero weights preserve SASRec rankings. Report every attempted configuration and its GPU seconds, including failures.

Cache validation branch scores only for the identical host-authorized pinned users/candidates; never regenerate negatives or replace the host evaluator. Compute per-user top-10 hits with its tie handling. Compare branch-only scores, transition-only and co-occurrence-only residuals, and the combined model. Report both-hit, SASRec-only-hit, branch-only-hit, neither-hit, ensemble rescues/regressions, nonzero target/candidate coverage, and HR@10 conditional on target coverage with denominators. Stratify descriptively using training-only item-popularity quartiles and history-length bins. A log1p(training interaction count) popularity-only ranking is a diagnostic control, not another blend parameter. These inspections do not authorize additional weight searches.

For uncertainty, use a dedicated seed-42 generator for 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates, independently resampling 200 users with replacement within each dataset. Reuse each sampled user's outcomes for both models, average the four dataset hit-rate differences, and report the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles and category deltas. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates and do not correct winner-selection optimism. Full-catalog simulator results for twenty real training users remain separate qualitative evidence; uncertain recommendations are not demonstrated dislikes.

As a budget-dependent follow-up, compare baseline single-negative BCE, BCE with 16 uniform negatives, and gBCE with the same 16 negatives, architecture, seeds, epochs, optimizer, and batch settings. Mask known training positives, never held-out labels. Fix the gBCE calibration parameter and its exact loss definition from the cited implementation before execution; record them, rather than silently treating gBCE as ordinary BCE. Run comparisons in that fixed order only when a measured runtime estimate fits the remaining budget. Then test the already selected residual configuration once on the strongest neural comparator; record this additional validation inspection. A hard-negative curriculum is a later hypothesis, not part of this initial residual experiment.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py loads identical category models, sparse tables, scales, recency parameters, and weights. Ensure candidate scores agree between batched candidate queries and full-catalog chunks. Expose the actual combined nn.Module as view.model, with frozen graph buffers or a module-owned sparse scorer. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Because the legacy feature-only scoring signature does not contain graph context, retain it for the neural compatibility path and add an explicit hybrid scoring method accepting both hidden features and their sequence prefixes. Adapt diagnostics to invoke that method; do not silently report neural-only margins as hybrid margins.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B×L. In eval mode without gradients, position t must use h_t and sequence[:t+1] for both target scores; mask padding and invalid positive/negative IDs. Report valid-pair count, mean positive/negative scores, mean and tenth-percentile margin, fraction margin<0, fraction margin<0.5, and pairwise accuracy defined as P(margin>0)+0.5P(margin=0). Define every output explicitly. Label embedding similarity as a neural-item-embedding diagnostic, and mark unavailable category breakdowns as unavailable rather than inventing categories.

Ordinary training-graph diagnostics can benefit from the diagnosed user's own target contributions. For an identifiable user, construct an additional graph-only exclusion view by subtracting ALL of that user's binary co-occurrence/support contributions and ALL chronological transition events, then recomputing affected cosine similarities, transition denominators, and top-K from unpruned counts. Rebuilding from retained neighbors alone is insufficient because excluded neighbors can enter top-K. Keep neural parameters, prefixes, candidate pairs, blend weights, and frozen score scales identical; the scales are explicitly not leave-one-user-out. This measures dependence on self-contributed graph associations, not full user exclusion or generalization. The anonymous loader requires an exact, unique match against known training sequence construction, or a separate identity-indexed diagnostic pass over public training histories. If identity cannot be recovered unambiguously or recomputation exceeds budget, report exclusion diagnostics as unavailable with the reason and evaluated-user count. Never guess identities or compare unmatched pairs. The interpreter prompt must use measured metrics and definitions and disclose training-target inclusion, exclusions, unavailable fields, and sampling limitations.
idea.pseudocode:
set_preprocessing_seed(0)
set_training_seed(42)
record_fixed_training_checkpoint_rule_and_shared_weight_grid()

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    neural = train_original_sasrec(category, configured_epochs_default=200)
    histories = chronological_training_histories(category)
    X = binary_deduplicated_user_item_incidence(histories)
    support = column_sum(X)
    co_counts = blockwise_sparse_product(X.T, X)
    cosine = co_counts / sqrt_outer_support_on_nonzeros(support)
    cosine = clear_diagonal(cosine)
    cosine = source_row_top_k(cosine, k=100)  # normalize before pruning

    transition_counts = adjacent_event_counts(histories, remove_self=True)
    transition = divide_by_full_source_row_sums(transition_counts)
    transition = source_row_top_k(transition, k=100)  # no post-prune renormalization
    scales = fit_training_only_branch_std(
        neural, transition, cosine,
        max_prefixes=10000, negatives_per_prefix=32, seed=42)
    save_category_artifacts_under_trial_directory()

    def hybrid_score(prefix, items, weights, hidden=None, graphs=None):
        recent = last_nonpadding_items(prefix, 10)
        recency = normalized_exp_weights(recent, decay_length=3)
        neural_score = neural.score(prefix, items, hidden=hidden)
        transition_score = weighted_outgoing_lookup(graphs.transition, recent, items, recency)
        cosine_score = weighted_outgoing_lookup(graphs.cosine, recent, items, recency)
        return (neural_score / scales.neural
                + weights.transition * transition_score / scales.transition
                + weights.cosine * cosine_score / scales.cosine)

cache_scores_only_on_host_authorized_identical_pinned_candidates()
weights = select_shared_grid_by_four_category_macro_hr10(
    tie_break='minimum total weight, then lexicographic')
report_branch_ablations_coverage_rescues_regressions_and_all_inspected_settings()
paired_stratified_bootstrap(replicates=2000, seed=42)

with evaluation_mode_and_no_grad():
    for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
        hidden = view.log2feats(sequence)
        for t in valid_target_positions(sequence, positive, negative):
            prefix = sequence[:, :t+1]
            pos_score = hybrid_score(prefix, positive[:, t], weights, hidden[:, t])
            neg_score = hybrid_score(prefix, negative[:, t], weights, hidden[:, t])
            accumulate_defined_pair_metrics(pos_score, neg_score)
            if user_identity_is_unambiguous_and_exclusion_fits_budget():
                excluded_graphs = rebuild_from_counts_without_all_user_contributions(user)
                score_identical_prefix_and_pair_with(excluded_graphs, fixed_scales=True)
            else:
                record_exclusion_unavailability()

write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_routing_and_hybrid_scoring()
verify_candidate_scores_match_full_catalog_chunk_scores()
return_diagnosis_metrics_and_metric_definitions()

originality.positive: The task-specific combination of recent personal context, directed transitions, and cosine neighborhoods produces a clear, falsifiable experiment.
originality.negative: ItemKNN, sequential rules, recency weighting, and score ensembles are established. Neither sparse graph construction nor blending alone supports a substantial novelty claim.

future_potential.positive: Evidence of complementary rescues and robustness to graph-only user exclusion could justify a later learned temporal gate or training-integrated collaborative branch.
future_potential.negative: Popularity shortcuts, sparse coverage, self-contributed associations, and validation selection optimism may explain apparent gains. Sampled HR@10 improvements may not transfer to full-catalog immediate-choice quality.

code_difficulty.positive: The ranking branch requires no additional neural architecture training and can use sparse counting and lookup.
code_difficulty.negative: Memory-bounded exact top-K construction, predictor parity, causal hybrid diagnostics, and correct user-contribution exclusion are materially more demanding than the original difficulty rating suggested.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention sequence encoder used as the starting model.
Establishes position-specific next-item scoring, motivating prefix-consistent hybrid diagnostics.
limitations: Implicit associations do not directly establish compatibility or current purchase need.
A causal attention mask does not prevent target inclusion through separately constructed graph statistics.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines global temporal item-transition information with a local Transformer.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this sparse residual on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: LS4SRec
contributions: Uses weighted global item-transition information while separating long- and short-term interests.
limitations: Motivates temporal collaborative evidence without validating this implementation or its compatibility-related effects.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Combines increased negative sampling with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
Motivates controlling negative count when comparing BCE and gBCE.
limitations: Does not establish that a transition ensemble improves this benchmark.
Loss calibration alone does not explicitly address stale interests and unsupported practical associations.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce model comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Provides an evaluation caution rather than evidence that the proposed model improves recommendations.

related_work.title: RecBole ItemKNN implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for interaction-based item similarities and neighborhood selection.
limitations: Implementation conventions must be specified explicitly; normalization and pruning order affect the resulting graph.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec neighborhood baselines
contributions: Provides established popularity-corrected co-occurrence baselines, including regularized cosine formulations.
limitations: Additional popularity exponents and shrinkage parameters would expand validation search; they are excluded from the initial fixed cosine recipe.

related_work.title: Sequential-rules implementation
contributions: Provides a reference for directed sequential associations and bounded-gap weighting.
limitations: The proposed initial branch uses adjacent events and explicitly specified row normalization rather than claiming to reproduce every sequential-rule variant.

related_work.title: Target-link inclusion study
contributions: Documents target-link inclusion concerns relevant to graph memorization and distribution shift.
limitations: Does not quantify contamination in this recommendation experiment; graph-only user exclusion remains a proposed diagnostic.

related_work.title: Candidate-sampling study
contributions: Motivates examining interactions between sampled candidates, popularity, and ranking conclusions.
limitations: Does not replace the pinned evaluator or establish full-catalog performance for this model.

related_work.title: Bootstrap evaluation in information retrieval
contributions: Provides a methodological basis for paired bootstrap uncertainty estimates.
limitations: The proposed dataset-stratified bootstrap conditions on fixed candidates and trained models and does not remove model-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated optimization of a validation criterion can overfit model selection.
limitations: A tiny declared grid limits search flexibility but does not make selected validation gains unbiased.
